elevationType.description: Elevation level granted for the approval. `admin` performs the elevation with admin rights; `user` keeps the action at the user level. Optional — defaults to the request's existing elevation type. Ignored for Technician Mode and Just-in-Time Log In requests.

createRule.description: When `true`, also create an auto-approval rule from this request so future matching elevations resolve automatically. Requires `ruleLevel`. Ignored for Technician Mode and Just-in-Time Log In requests.

ruleLevel.description: Scope at which an auto-created rule applies: `computer`, `location`, `company`, or `msp` (all companies). Required when `createRule` is `true`.

durationInMinutes.description: Length of the resulting session in minutes. Required when the request is an elevated-session request — omitting it answers 422. Ignored for every other request type. A value outside 1 to 60 answers 400. An Addigy-managed Mac raises the floor to 10, and a value under it answers 422, because only the request says which provider runs the session.

companyIds.description: Allow-list: the only companies this user can see.
Deny-list: every company in the MSP except these.

CompanyAccessInput.description: Company access to write. `some` and `most` require a non-empty `companyIds`; `all` and `none` must not carry one. Every id must be a company of the authenticated partner's MSP that the token can access; any other id is answered with 404, as a resource in another tenant does not exist for this token.

lastName.description: Family name. Optional; defaults to an empty string.

email.description: Sign-in address. Must be unique across the platform — a duplicate is rejected with 409.

roleId.description: Role to assign. Must be a role in the authenticated partner's MSP — see `GET /api/roles`.

technicianModeTicketingEnabled.description: Whether the user may use technician-mode ticketing.

sendInvitationEmail.description: When `true` (the default), the platform emails the new user a link to set their initial password — without it they have no way to sign in. Set `false` to create the record silently and invite them later from the Admin Portal.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint payloads are delivered to. A read returns this redacted to its origin, and that redacted form is not accepted here — send the full URL, or omit the field to keep the stored one.

eventSubscriptions.description: Event types to subscribe to. At least one is required; duplicates are collapsed. The `user.*` events need an MSP-wide webhook (no `companyId`); combining them with a `companyId` is rejected.

companyId.description: Scope the webhook to a single company. Omit to receive events for all of the MSP's companies. A company-scoped webhook is not re-pointed when that company is merged away or removed — re-scope or delete it as part of that change.

createRule.description: When `true`, also create a denial rule from this request so future matching elevations are auto-denied. Requires `ruleLevel`. Ignored for Technician Mode and Just-in-Time Log In requests.

ruleLevel.description: Scope at which an auto-created rule applies: `computer`, `location`, `company`, or `msp` (all companies). Required when `createRule` is `true`.

denialReason.description: Free-text reason for the denial, shown to the end user on their machine alongside the denial notification. Plain text; maximum 1000 characters.

EditableRuleElevationType.description: Elevation level applied when this rule auto-approves a matching event. `admin` elevates with admin rights; `user` keeps the action at the user level.

enabled.description: `true` queues technician mode on for the computer, `false` queues it off.

SettableElevationMode.description: Elevation mode to apply on a computer: `audit`, `live` or `policy` — the same three the Admin Portal offers — or `inherit`, which drops the per-computer override so the computer follows the mode set at its location, company or MSP.

approved.description: When `true`, matching elevations are auto-approved; when `false`, they are auto-denied.

shouldIgnore.description: When `true`, the agent treats matching events as audit-mode and does not prompt to elevate.

friendlyName.description: Human-readable name for the rule. Pass `null` to clear it.

notes.description: Free-text notes describing the rule. Pass `null` to clear it.

identificationCriteria.description: Opaque criteria the agent matches against incoming events to decide whether this rule applies. Shape is intentionally not part of the public contract — supply the same structure the read endpoint returns. Omit to leave the criteria unchanged; anything but an object (including `null`) is rejected because a rule needs criteria to match anything.

lastName.description: Family name. Pass an empty string to clear it.

roleId.description: Role to assign. Must be a role in the authenticated partner's MSP — see `GET /api/roles`.

technicianModeTicketingEnabled.description: Whether the user may use technician-mode ticketing.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint payloads are delivered to. A read returns this redacted to its origin, and that redacted form is not accepted here — send the full URL, or omit the field to keep the stored one.

eventSubscriptions.description: Replacement set of subscribed event types; duplicates are collapsed.

allOf.description: Change the delivery format for this webhook.

enabled.description: Enable or disable deliveries for this webhook.

companyId.description: Re-scope the webhook to a company, or `null` to widen it to all of the MSP's companies. A company scope is rejected while the webhook subscribes to any `user.*` event.

WebhookEventType.description: An event type a webhook can subscribe to. The `test` type is never subscribable — it is reserved for deliveries triggered via the test endpoint.

WebhookFormat.description: How the payload is delivered. `native` sends the signed `WebhookEventEnvelope` JSON. `teams-incoming-webhook` sends an Adaptive Card for a Microsoft Teams inbound webhook (point it at a Power Automate Workflows URL). `slack-incoming-webhook` sends a Block Kit message for a Slack inbound webhook. Only `native` carries an `X-AutoElevate-Signature` — Teams and Slack cannot verify it.
